pages.title: Three Parallel Lanes
pages.text: The Immortal Furnace has three independent processing lanes. TruePower mode handles one item per lane in 50 ticks; ImmortalPower mode handles a whole stack per lane in 25. The placed and stage-five embedded furnaces share recipes and processing rules.

pages.title: The Right Column
pages.text: From top to bottom: $(item)reinforcement plugin$(), cyan-white flame, fuel. The plugin slot accepts one dimensional plugin; the flame shows burn remaining; fuel accepts TruePower, ImmortalPower or a claimed Spirit Drive. A blocked lane pauses independently without consuming input.

pages.title: Plugins Only Accelerate
pages.text: Dimensional Peeking Order, Parallel Talisman and Great-Thousand-World Edict provide 4×, 16× and 256× progress. Each $(thing)advances processing only$(): output per recipe stays fixed and fuel burn ticks never change. Placed and embedded furnaces behave identically.

pages.title: Fuel and Refill
pages.text: TruePower smelts 10 items; ImmortalPower smelts 500. Inside its owner's realm, a furnace may refill ImmortalPower from that owner. With a Spirit Drive inserted, it pays the drive owner in ImmortalPower first and TruePower second. The drive is a reusable credential, never burned.

pages.title: Embedded Furnace
pages.text: The embedded furnace refills another complete copy of the previous input stack from Xianqiao and returns results directly to storage. Plugins are neither refilled nor exported. If an output cannot fit in full, that lane waits. See $(l:immortalstorage:recipes/immortal_furnace_processes)Immortal Furnace Catalogue$(/l) for all 11 recipes.

pages.title: The Personal Realm
pages.text: From stage six, the realm follows the persistent ImmortalStorage identity rather than the launcher's current session UUID. Saves from 0.0.8 or earlier migrate only from reliable evidence such as the old realm or a consistent bound item; otherwise the old directory is preserved, never guessed over.

pages.title: Time, Weather and Boundary
pages.text: Stage controls the playable boundary and time gears. The management page selects noon or midnight and cycles clear, rain, thunder or snow, affecting only the owner's realm. Crossing the boundary gives notice and returns the player to the nearest legal point.
